As part of our commitment to innovation and excellence, the Commercial Team is currently undertaking TOPlytics, a transformative project to redesign drilling operations for the 21st century. This project encompasses data management, digitalization, business improvement, and strategic transformation.   Job Summary :  We are seeking a talented and motivated Data Analyst to join our team in Kalgoorlie at our head office. As a Data Analyst, you will play a crucial and highly visible role in our TOPlytics project, collaborating closely with business stakeholders to understand their challenges and provide data-driven solutions. You will work on a variety of data projects, including creating and managing workflows and data models, developing impactful dashboards, and conducting analysis. Your insights and contributions will directly contribute to improving safety, enhancing operational efficiency, and driving profitability within our drilling operations.   Responsibilities:    Adhere to and monitor the daily, weekly, and monthly tasks associated with the position, ensuring compliance with updated requirements.  Maintain, optimize, and troubleshoot existing workflows and data models.  Create and maintain dashboards for data analysis and reporting.  Design and implement automation to streamline repetitive tasks.  Train end-users on new reports and dashboards, collaborating with stakeholders to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the displayed information and its significance in supporting data-driven decision making.  Educate stakeholders on the meaning and context of the data presented, emphasizing how it can be leveraged to make informed business decisions. Provide project reporting, including activities, achievements, delays, and updates on a daily, weekly, fortnightly, and monthly basis.  Commission and decommission data sets.  Manage and design the reporting environment, including data sources, security, and metadata.  Assess and implement new or upgraded software, contributing to strategic decisions on new systems.  Provide technical expertise in data storage structures, data mining, and data cleansing.  Travel to various client sites throughout WA & NT when required.  Present analysis to users with low technical background.  Conduct Tableau on-boarding for new users.  Conducting Exploratory Data Analysis.    Qualifications and Experience:    A tertiary qualification in Economics, Commerce, Engineering, Data Science, and/or Computer Science, or currently studying in these fields.  1-3 years of experience in a similar data analyst role.    Technical Skills:    Proficiency in Tableau and SQL is essential.  Undrestand Data modeling.  Python or R is good to know, but not essential.  dbt knowledge is a significant advantage.  Understand EDA.  Prior experience with SQL.  Demonstrated experience in handling large data sets and relational databases.  Proficiency in Microsoft Office, with advanced skills in Excel.    Personal Skills:    Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.  Excellent communication skills with the ability to effectively convey insights through data.  A strong understanding of digital and data trends, with a passion for leveraging new technology to solve business problems.  Commercial mindset with a focus on operational efficiency.  Highly organized with excellent time management skills.  Reliable, self-motivated, and able to maintain confidentiality.  Enthusiastic and proactive approach to work, displaying a desire to learn and a commitment to task completion.  High-level written and verbal communication skills.      At Topdrill, we value diversity and encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds. We appreciate all applications, but only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.  About Company     Topdrill has come a long way from its humble beginnings in a small yard in Kalgoorlie, Western Australia. Tim Topham started with a single drill rig, building the company into a widely respected group of exploration drilling professionals that successfully partners with Australia's top tier miners.    We are driven to be your number one exploration drilling partner of choice. Not only are we focused on investing in and maintaining our superior equipment fleet, but are continuously improving our drilling services to offer the best value for our clients. Our innovative drilling solutions focus on safety and high-quality sample and production outcomes. result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Data Architect





Job no: 944478

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide CBD

Categories: Information-Communication Technology, Public Health, Research and Data Analysis




 

The Commission on Excellence and Innovation in Health (CEIH) - Clinical Informatics and Innovation Directorate (CIID) - SACCaN D&I (South Australian Comprehensive Cancer Network Data and Intelligence)

Salary: $130,046 to $134,956 - ASO8 - Full Time - Term Contract up to 12 Months

Overview:

The Data Architect provides strategic leadership in the design, development and governance of a complex, patient-centric enterprise data architecture, including a data lakehouse, multiple analytical platforms, and associated data integration and interoperability requirements. The role ensures that high-value clinical, operational and research data assets are usable, trusted, secure and fit for purpose to support the objectives of the SA Cancer Network.

The Data Architect interprets complex business, clinical and information requirements and translates them into conceptual, logical, and physical data architectures, data models and standards. Working collaboratively with clinicians, the CEIH Clinical Informatics and Innovation Directorate (CIID), solution architects and other stakeholders, the role ensures a consistent, interoperable, and standards-based approach to data design across systems, platforms and agencies.

The role leads the definition, implementation and continuous improvement of data architecture frameworks, standards, patterns, and best practices, including lakehouse design, data modelling, metadata management, master and reference data, and data integration approaches. The Data Architect provides architectural assurance to ensure data solutions align with enterprise architecture, agreed Digital Health and CIID standards, and whole-of-government data and digital strategies.

The Data Architect works collaboratively with delivery teams, customers, and stakeholders to understand data and information needs, providing authoritative technical consultancy and design guidance to inform solution options, platform adoption and investment decisions. The role ensures that data architectures enable advanced analytics, reporting, research, and insight generation as well as supporting patient-centric care models.

The CIID values innovation, excellence, collaboration, knowledge sharing, transparency, accountability, and respect.

The Commission on Excellence and Innovation in Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and appropriate immunisation requirements.

Job ref: 944478

Criminal History Screening Requirement

A 'National Police Certificate' NPC (also known as a 'Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check' NCCHC) for employment involving no contact with vulnerable groups is required for this position (general employment).

A DHS 'Working With Children Check' (WWCC) is required for this position.

Immunisation Risk for this position is Category C (minimal patient contact).

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

Various - full time, part time, ongoing and temporary contracts will be available through the pool.

About the role

Join our Microbiology team as a Medical Scientist (MeS-1) and begin an exciting career journey in a dynamic diagnostic laboratory environment. This role provides the opportunity to apply your scientific knowledge and technical skills while contributing to the delivery of accurate, reliable and high-quality pathology services that support patient care. Under appropriate guidance and supervision, you will perform a range of routine microbiology diagnostic techniques, participate in the testing process from planning through to reporting, and develop your expertise in laboratory practices, quality processes and scientific methodologies.

As an important member of our multidisciplinary team, you will work alongside experienced scientists, technical staff and medical professionals to support the delivery of exceptional laboratory services. You will have opportunities to build your professional capability through competency-based training, contribute to teaching and research activities, and assist with the development and implementation of new techniques and approaches. This role offers a supportive environment where you can grow your skills, strengthen your professional judgement and progress your career within medical science.

About you

You are an enthusiastic and dedicated Medical Scientist with a passion for diagnostic microbiology and a commitment to delivering accurate, high-quality pathology services. You will bring a strong foundation in laboratory science, a willingness to learn and develop your skills, and a collaborative approach to supporting a positive and professional team environment.

Qualified and developing scientist - You hold an appropriate Medical Science qualification recognised under NPAAC requirements and have an understanding of diagnostic microbiology, infectious diseases and general pathology laboratory practices.

Quality focused and technically capable - You have the ability to perform routine diagnostic testing, follow laboratory procedures, operate and troubleshoot equipment, apply scientific principles and contribute to the delivery of accurate and reliable results.

Organised and proactive team member - You can prioritise workloads, manage time effectively, work with increasing independence, identify potential issues and use initiative while contributing positively within a multidisciplinary laboratory team.

Effective communicator with a commitment to service - You demonstrate strong communication skills, maintain confidentiality, provide professional customer service and build positive working relationships with scientific, technical and clinical colleagues.

About us

Statewide Clinical Support Services (SCSS) is a unique public healthcare organisation that serves health consumers and provides specialist clinical services to the health system in South Australia. SCSS encompasses BreastScreen SA, SA Dental, SA Medical Imaging, SA Pathology, and SA Pharmacy. Come and work with us to improve the health and well-being of South Australians, across all age groups and at any time of their life or health need. 

What we offer

Salary Benefits: Enjoy flexible salary packaging options, including up to $9,010 each FBT year for living expenses (such as mortgage, rent, utilities and groceries) plus an additional $2,650 for meal and entertainment expenses.

Professional Development: Opportunity to apply for reimbursement of eligible professional development activities, and access to dedicated leave for ongoing learning.

Annual Leave: Enjoy paid recreation leave for essential rejuvenation, with leave loading applied.

Health and Fitness Benefits: Access to Fitness Passport, a discounted workplace health and fitness program for you and your family, plus an annual voluntary flu vaccination to support your wellbeing.

Employee Assistance Program: Confidential counselling and support services for you and your family via our Employee Assistance Program.

Diversity and inclusion:

Statewide supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe at work. The culture aims to encourage all people to use their talents and to be valued and rewarded for their contributions.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants are encouraged to apply.

Please refer to the role description for essential educational-vocational qualifications that may be required.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and compliant Immunisation screening as indicated in the role description.

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

Geographic Information System (GIS) Analyst

Kogan People Solutions are delighted to be working with a local government powerhouse in Melbourne’s southeast, who wish to appoint a qualified skilled and experienced Geographic Information System (GIS) Analyst.

The newly appointed Geographic Information System (GIS) Analyst will coordinate the collection, maintenance, and reporting of Council’s GIS and spatial databases to ensure a "single source of truth" enhance spatial systems to support business units, optimize data integration for modelling, and deliver GIS training and support across the organization.

Location – Dandenong Vic

Employment Type: Full-time, Ongoing

Salary – Offered in the range $95k to $105k plus superannuation, per annum 

Key Responsibilities of this exciting position include

System Development & Management

•	Platform Administration: Manage and enhance QGIS, IntraMaps, Mapbox, and related spatial systems to expand corporate utility.

•	Integration: Integrate GIS with corporate databases, the Property Information System, and Asset Management Systems to ensure data quality and system functionality.

•	Data Governance: Coordinate spatial data collection (including GPS data) and ensure compliance with external data agreements.
Business Analysis & Reporting

•	Data Interrogation: Utilize GIS and SQL query tools to extract, analyze, and interrogate spatial data for ad-hoc business requirements.

•	Reporting & Presentation: Create, map, and professionally present spatial and textual information for performance reporting and publications.

Customer Support & Vendor Management

•	Support & Training: Provide technical support, document user requests, prepare training materials, and deliver non-technical GIS training to internal staff.

•	Collaboration: Facilitate the bi-monthly GIS User Group and maintain effective working relationships with software vendors and contractors.
Continuous Improvement & Governance

•	Process Optimization: Review GIS workflows via process mapping and assist in developing industry-best-practice policies and procedures.

•	Change Management: Adhere to operational procedures for IT services, focusing on system testing and change management principles.

To be considered, we expect to be able to observe:

Education and Professional Memberships

•	Degree Qualification: Bachelor’s degree in GIS, Computer Science, or a relevant IT field.

•	Professional Association: Membership (or eligibility for membership) with a professional geospatial body requiring Continuing Professional Development (CPD), such as the Geospatial Council of Australia (formerly SSSI) or GITA.

Technical Skills & Experience

•	GIS & Database Admin: Proven experience developing, implementing, and administering GIS systems, SQL servers, and databases (Local Government experience preferred).

•	Data Querying: Demonstrated ability to interrogate complex spatial data using spatialized SQL queries.

•	Analytical & Communication Skills: Strong problem-solving capabilities, paired with the ability to communicate technical GIS concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

Mandatory Licences & Pre-Employment Checks

The following credentials must be held (or obtained) prior to commencement and maintained throughout employment:

•	Current valid Victorian Driver’s Licence

•	Satisfactory National Police Check

•	Satisfactory Working with Children Check (WWCC)
